svg.title: The Donkey and Her Prophet
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (Numbers 22:7, 17-18): at dawn, two princes of Moab hold out gifts to Balaam, who stands beside his saddled donkey with his staff. Caption: "Pethor, by the Euphrates. Balak, king of Moab, has sent princes with the fees for divination." A prince of Moab says: "Come, curse this people for me." Balaam says: "I could not go beyond the command of the LORD my God". Panel 2 (Numbers 22:22-25): on a narrow path between vineyards with a low stone wall, Balaam rides the donkey and raises his staff to strike her; ahead stands the angel of the LORD as light with a drawn sword. Caption: "Between the vineyards." Numbers says: "the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road, with a drawn sword in his hand." Panel 3 (Numbers 22:27-28): the donkey lying down on the path, Balaam standing over her with his staff raised; the angel's light stands ahead; the donkey speaks to him. Caption: "The third time she lies down. Then the LORD opens her mouth." The donkey says: "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?" Panel 4 (Numbers 22:31-35): Balaam kneels on the road before the angel's light and drawn sword; the donkey stands behind him. Caption: "Then the LORD opens Balaam's eyes." Balaam says: "I have sinned". The angel of the LORD says: "Go with the men, but speak only the word that I tell you." Panel 5 (Numbers 23:7-8): Balaam stands on a height at dawn with his arms open, looking down toward the camp, which lies out of the picture. Caption: "On the heights above Israel's camp." Balaam says: "How can I curse whom God has not cursed?" The point: No one can curse those God has blessed. The LORD who opened a donkey's mouth and a prophet's eyes turned the curse into a blessing, because He loves His people (Deuteronomy 23:5), and in Jesus that blessing is yours (Galatians 3:14).
svg.text: A hired curse that God would not let him speak, in one minute

g.text: king of Moab, has sent princes
The third time she lies down.
Then the LORD opens her mouth.

svg.text: No one can curse those God has blessed. The LORD who opened
a donkey's mouth and a prophet's eyes turned the curse into
a blessing, because He loves His people (Deuteronomy 23:5),
and in Jesus that blessing is yours (Galatians 3:14).
The angel of the LORD is drawn as light holding the drawn sword Numbers gives him (22:23); the text
gives no form. The donkey is a she-donkey (Hebrew aton). Balak is named in the story but not drawn.
